title: Volatility-adjusted yield: income per unit of realized risk
summary: The speaker's volatility-adjusted yield (VAY) divides option income by realized volatility. Two covered calls both yield 3% a month, but one stock realizes 28% volatility and the other 10%. The one at 10% is the better trade per unit of risk. He says this beats IV rank and IV percentile.

steps.caption: A stock path. We sell covered calls on it for a 3% monthly yield.
Realized volatility here is about 10%. Another stock with the same 3% yield realizes 28%.
Implied volatility sets the option price. IV rank only compares IV with its own past.
The gap from IV to realized volatility is the edge. 3% on 10% realized is much more income per unit of risk.
Main idea: divide yield by realized volatility before you compare two income trades.

takeaways: Equal yields do not mean equal trades; normalize by realized volatility.
3% on a stock that realizes 10% beats 3% on one that realizes 28%.
IV rank and IV percentile compare IV only with itself.
caveats: VAY (volatility-adjusted yield) is the speaker's own metric, sold through his tools. It is unverified here.
The follower testimonial and free Chrome extension are promotional.
